0.title: Widgets
0.content: A widget puts live data on the dashboard. There are two kinds, as in homepage: . | Service widgets go on a service’s card in services.yaml, under widget: (or widgets: for several). They show the numbers of that service: the queue of Radarr, the blocked queries of Pi-hole, the VMs of Proxmox. # services.yaml - Media: - Radarr: href: http://radarr.lan icon: radarr.svg widget: type: radarr url: http://radarr.lan:7878 key: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_RADARR_KEY}}" . | Header widgets go in the page’s header, in widgets.yaml: the date and time, system resources, search, the weather. # widgets.yaml - openmeteo: label: Amsterdam latitude: 52.37 longitude: 4.89 . | . Every widget below comes from the widgets collection, which is always installed. Missing one? Any widget package can be added under plugins:: the Catalogue lists packages by others, and Extend shows how to write your own.

2.content: | Widget | type | What it shows | . | Date and time | datetime | The current date and time, formatted for the dashboard language. | . | Greeting | greeting | A line of text in the header, as in homepage’s greeting widget. | . | Kubernetes | kubernetes | CPU and memory of a Kubernetes cluster (the one the dashboard runs in, or kubernetes.yaml’s kubeconfig), in total and per node (homepage’s kubernetes widget). | . | Logo | logo | A logo in the header: the dashboard’s own mark, or an icon of your choice, as in homepage. | . | Open-Meteo | openmeteo | The current weather from Open-Meteo, no account needed (homepage’s recommended weather widget). | . | OpenWeatherMap | openweathermap | The current weather from OpenWeatherMap, with your API key or a shared provider (homepage’s openweathermap widget). | . | System resources | resources | CPU, memory, disk, CPU temperature, uptime and network of the machine (or container) the dashboard runs on, as meters like homepage. | . | Search | search | Filters the dashboard’s services as you type; Enter opens the only match, or searches the web. | . | Stocks | stocks | The price and day change of up to eight stocks, from Finnhub (homepage’s stocks widget). | .

4.title: AdGuard Home
4.content: type: adguard · version 0.3.2 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . DNS queries, queries blocked by the filter lists, queries filtered by Safe Browsing, Safe Search and parental control, and the average processing time, as homepage’s adguard widget. Over the statistics period set in AdGuard Home (Settings > General settings > Statistics). username and password are the login of AdGuard Home’s web interface. Learn more about AdGuard Home.

5.title: Display fields
5.content: queries, blocked, filtered, latency . Pick them with fields: in the entry.

6.title: Configuration options
6.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | url | url | yes |   | E.g. http://adguard.lan:3000 | . | username | string |   |   | The web interface login | . | password | string |   |   | Secret: stays on the server. | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

7.title: Filter attributes
7.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | queries | number | DNS queries answered | . | blocked | number | DNS queries blocked by the filter lists | . | filtered | number | Queries replaced by Safe Browsing, Safe Search or parental control | . | latency | number | Average processing time of a query, in ms | .

8.title: Example
8.content: # services.yaml - Network: - AdGuard Home: href: http://adguard.lan:3000 icon: adguard-home widget: type: adguard fields: [queries, blocked, filtered, latency] # the display fields; leave out for the defaults url: http://adguard.lan:3000 username: admin password: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_ADGUARD_PASSWORD}}" .

10.title: APC UPS
10.content: type: apcups · version 0.4.0 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . Status (on battery and a lost connection marked), load, battery charge and runtime left of an APC UPS, read from apcupsd’s network information server, as homepage’s apcups widget. apcupsd listens on 127.0.0.1 by default: set NISIP in /etc/apcupsd.conf to an address the dashboard can reach (and keep NETSERVER on), then restart apcupsd. url is that address and port, tcp://host:3551. Learn more about apcupsd.

11.title: Display fields
11.content: status, load, bcharge, timeleft . Pick them with fields: in the entry.

12.title: Configuration options
12.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | url | string | yes |   | Apcupsd’s network server, e.g. tcp://nas.lan:3551 | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

13.title: Filter attributes
13.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | status | string | The UPS’s state: online, onBattery or lost | . | load | number | Load on the UPS, in % of its capacity | . | bcharge | number | Battery charge, in % | . | timeleft | number | Minutes the battery lasts at the current load | . | attention | boolean | True while the card marks something as needing attention | .

14.title: Example
14.content: # services.yaml - Infrastructure: - UPS: icon: apc widget: type: apcups fields: [status, load, bcharge, timeleft] # the display fields; leave out for the defaults url: tcp://nas.lan:3551 .

16.title: Arcane
16.content: type: arcane · version 0.3.1 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . Containers running, stopped and in total, and images with an update (marked), as homepage’s arcane widget; the number of images, used and unused through fields. Make an API key in Arcane with the permissions containers:list, images:list and image-updates:read. env is the environment id (0 is the local one). Learn more about Arcane.

17.title: Display fields
17.content: running, stopped, total, image_updates, images, images_used, images_unused . Pick them with fields: in the entry; without it the widget shows running, stopped, total, image_updates.

18.title: Configuration options
18.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | url | url | yes |   | E.g. http://arcane.lan:3552 | . | key | string | yes |   | Secret: stays on the server. An API key with containers:list, images:list and image-updates:read | . | env | string |   | 0 | The environment id; 0 is Arcane’s local one | . 88.title: Button
88.content: type: button · version 1.5.2 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . A button on a card or in the header that opens a link, or runs a script or a shell command on the dashboard’s server, for jobs such as pulling new images, restarting a stack or starting a backup. Set exactly one of href, script or command; with none or several, the card shows an error. | href opens the page in a new tab. | script runs a file with bash. A relative path is relative to the config folder (/config in the container), which is also the folder the run starts in. | command runs a line with bash -c, such as docker compose -f stacks/media.yaml pull. | . While it runs, the button shows a spinner instead of its label and cannot be pressed. A run that succeeds (exit code 0) shows a check for a moment, then the label again. A run that fails opens the dashboard’s result dialog with the output (stdout and stderr together, the last 64 kB) and the exit code; the output can be copied from there. A run that takes longer than timeout seconds (default 300) is stopped, together with everything it started. Values filled in from {{DASHBOARD_VAR_*}} are scrubbed from the output. The run gets only PATH and HOME from the dashboard’s environment; set inheritEnv: true to pass all of it, except the DASHBOARD_VAR_* and DASHBOARD_FILE_* variables when the button runs in the dashboard’s widget worker (the default). Give a script a value in its command instead: command: TOKEN={{DASHBOARD_VAR_TOKEN}} scripts/deploy.sh. It runs as the dashboard’s user (node, uid 1000, in the image), so tools such as curl, jq or docker must be in the image and the Docker socket must allow that user. Running as root . user: root runs the script as root inside the container, for a script that writes files which must stay owned by root (a proxy’s config, chown). It needs DASHBOARD_ALLOW_ROOT_SCRIPTS: "true" in the dashboard container’s environment; without it the button says so. The dashboard itself keeps running as node: the image lets it start one fixed runner as root through sudo, and only when that variable is set. HOME is then /root; inheritEnv: true passes the dashboard’s environment to the root script too. A timeout stops the root script and what it started. Once the variable is on, any installed widget could run as root in the container, so set it only on a dashboard you trust. Anyone who can open the dashboard can press the button: put the dashboard behind authentication before you add buttons that change things. script and command are kept on the server; the browser only gets the label. script, command, user and inheritEnv are only taken from services.yaml: a button found through Docker labels or Kubernetes annotations can open a link, but runs nothing (the dashboard names the label in its messages). Labels are written by whoever starts a container, or come with its image. Asking for a password . With an admin password on the dashboard (adminPassword in its settings.yaml, which its setup wizard and settings page write), a press can ask for that password first. A button with user: root asks by default; any button asks with confirm: password (then that browser stays unlocked for a while, 15 minutes by default) or confirm: always (every press). confirm: none turns it off for a root button. Without an admin password nothing asks, and the dashboard’s messages name the buttons that would. See the dashboard’s Admin password. With the dashboard’s login page (login: true) a login counts: only confirm: always asks again. Several buttons on one card are several button widgets, each one full width.

89.title: Display fields
89.content: No blocks: the button is drawn by the widget.

90.title: Configuration options
90.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | text | string | yes |   | The button’s label | . | href | url |   |   | Opens this page in a new tab, e.g. https://grafana.lan/ | . | script | string |   |   | Secret: stays on the server. A bash script to run, e.g. scripts/update.sh (relative to the config folder) | . | command | string |   |   | Secret: stays on the server. A shell command to run with bash -c, e.g. docker compose pull | . | timeout | number |   | 300 | Seconds before the run is stopped | . | inheritEnv | boolean |   | false | Give the run the dashboard’s environment (without DASHBOARD_VAR_*), not only PATH and HOME | . | user | node / root |   | node | Root needs DASHBOARD_ALLOW_ROOT_SCRIPTS=true on the dashboard container | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

91.title: Filter attributes
91.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | attention | boolean | True while the card marks something as needing attention | .

100.title: Calendar
100.content: type: calendar · version 0.3.0 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . A month with a coloured dot per event and the chosen day’s events below it, or with view: agenda a list of the coming events, as homepage’s calendar widget. Events come from integrations: Sonarr (episodes), Radarr (cinema, physical and digital releases), Lidarr (albums) and Readarr (books), and any iCal feed (Google Calendar, Nextcloud, …). Use the arrows to page through months; done items (a file is there) are dimmed, and items link to baseUrl when it is set. An integration of an *arr points to a service on the dashboard with service_group and service_name, as in homepage: the dashboard fills in that widget’s url and key on the server. Or give url and key yourself. params: { unmonitored: true } also shows unmonitored items. An iCal integration takes the feed’s url and a name (params: { showName: true } puts it before each title); for Google Calendar use Settings > your calendar > Integrate calendar > Secret address in iCal format. Repeating events are expanded (daily, weekly with days, monthly, yearly; with INTERVAL, COUNT, UNTIL and EXDATE). timezone sets the zone the days are counted in (default the viewer’s). showTime: true shows the time of today’s events. Learn more about iCalendar.

150.content: type: custom-api (or customapi) · version 1.3.0 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . Shows fields from any JSON API without writing a widget, like homepage’s customapi. 182.title: Docker container
182.content: type: docker · version 1.8.0 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . State, CPU and memory of one container. This is the widget behind a service’s container:, which reads the server from docker.yaml; used directly, it takes a socket or a url. The dashboard only reads from Docker. Give it a docker-socket-proxy with CONTAINERS=1 rather than the socket itself: see Discovery. A Docker daemon over TLS (port 2376) is set up in docker.yaml with tls: { caFile, certFile, keyFile } (see Configuration); the dashboard fills in tlsCa, tlsCert and tlsKey for container: from those files. With swarm: true (set from docker.yaml’s swarm: true for container:), a name that is no container is looked up as a Swarm service: its running tasks against the replicas (replicas), marked when only some run. attention is true while the container is unhealthy (its Docker healthcheck), stopped or not found, so a service can hide its card while all is well: filter: container.attention == false reads it from the service’s container:.

183.title: Display fields
183.content: status, replicas, cpu, memory, rx, tx (data received and sent over the container’s networks, as homepage’s RX and TX) . Pick them with fields: in the entry.

184.title: Configuration options
184.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | container | string | yes |   |   | . | socket | string |   |   | Default /var/run/docker.sock | . | url | url |   |   | A Docker API or docker-socket-proxy, instead of a socket | . | swarm | boolean |   | false | Also look for a Swarm service of that name (docker.yaml swarm: true) | . | tlsCa | string |   |   | Secret: stays on the server. PEM text; filled in from docker.yaml tls.caFile | . | tlsCert | string |   |   | Secret: stays on the server. PEM text; filled in from docker.yaml tls.certFile | . | tlsKey | string |   |   | Secret: stays on the server. PEM text; filled in from docker.yaml tls.keyFile | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

185.title: Filter attributes
185.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | status | string | Up, warn (unhealthy) or down, as the status label | . | attention | boolean | True while the container is unhealthy, stopped or not found (container.attention) | .

186.title: Example
186.content: # services.yaml - Media: - Plex: href: http://plex.lan:32400 container: plex # state label in the corner, from docker.yaml widget: type: docker fields: [status, replicas, cpu, memory, rx, tx] # the display fields; leave out for the defaults container: plex url: http://socket-proxy:2375 .

266.title: FRITZ!Box
266.content: type: fritzbox · version 0.4.0 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . 302.title: Glances
302.content: type: glances · version 0.4.0 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . CPU, memory, CPU temperature, uptime and disks of a machine that runs Glances in web server mode (glances -w, port 61208). Set version: 4 for Glances 4 or later. Give username and password only when Glances runs with --password. cputemp takes the hottest CPU sensor (labels starting with cpu_thermal, Core, Tctl, Temperature or Package id; add your own with cpuSensorLabel) and is marked from 85 °C. disk takes mount points as Glances lists them. CPU temperature, uptime and disks are off by default because each takes an extra call, as in homepage. Learn more about Glances.

303.content: cpu, memory, memoryUsed, memoryTotal, cputemp, uptime, disk (one mount point) or one per mount point named after it, diskFree . Pick them with fields: in the entry; without it the widget shows cpu, memory, cputemp, uptime.

Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

348.content: type: homeassistant · version 0.3.0 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . People at home, lights that are on and switches that are on (each as “on / all”), as homepage’s homeassistant widget. With custom, up to four entries of your own instead, in homepage’s form: . | state: <entity_id> shows that entity. label defaults to {attributes.friendly_name}, value to {state} {attributes.unit_of_measurement}; both may name other attributes in braces. | template: <Jinja template> shows what Home Assistant renders, with your label. | . Make a long-lived access token in Home Assistant: your profile (bottom left) > Security > Long-lived access tokens > Create token. The token can read everything its user can. Learn more about Home Assistant.

A long-lived access token: your profile > Security | . | custom | list |   |   |   | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

351.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | peopleHome | number | People at home (without custom) | . | lightsOn | number | Lights that are on (without custom) | . | switchesOn | number | Switches that are on (without custom) | . | custom1 | string | The first custom entry’s value, as the card shows it (e.g. “on”, “21.5 °C”) | . | custom2 | string | The second custom entry’s value | . | custom3 | string | The third custom entry’s value | . | custom4 | string | The fourth custom entry’s value | .

372.title: iFrame
372.content: type: iframe · version 1.1.0 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . Another page in a frame on the card, as homepage’s iframe widget: a Grafana panel, a camera page, a status page. The dashboard allows the page’s origin (scheme, host and port of src) in its Content-Security-Policy; every other origin stays blocked. Your browser loads the page itself, so it must be reachable from the browser, and the page must allow being framed (no X-Frame-Options: DENY or frame-ancestors that leaves the dashboard out). height sets the frame’s height (default 15rem); homepage’s classes are read for their height (h-60 is 15rem, the last h-<n> counts). allowScrolling: no makes the page a picture that cannot be scrolled or clicked, and refreshInterval reloads it every so many milliseconds.

373.title: Display fields
373.content: No blocks: the frame is drawn by the widget.

374.title: Configuration options
374.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | src | url | yes |   | The page, e.g. https://grafana.lan/d-solo/abc?panelId=2 | . | name | string |   |   | The frame’s title for screen readers | . | height | string |   |   | A CSS height, e.g. 20rem (default 15rem) | . | classes | string |   |   | Homepage’s Tailwind height classes; the h- of the largest screen is used | . | referrerPolicy | string |   |   | E.g. same-origin | . | allowPolicy | string |   |   | The frame’s allow attribute, e.g. autoplay; fullscreen | . | allowFullscreen | boolean |   | true |   | . | allowfullscreen | boolean |   |   | Homepage’s spelling of allowFullscreen | . | loadingStrategy | eager / lazy |   | eager |   | . | allowScrolling | yes / no |   | yes | No: the page cannot be scrolled or clicked | . | refreshInterval | number |   |   | Reload the page every this many milliseconds (at least 1000) | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

375.title: Example
375.content: # services.yaml - Monitoring: - Power use: widget: type: iframe name: Power use src: https://grafana.lan/d-solo/power?orgId=1&panelId=2 height: 12rem allowScrolling: "no" refreshInterval: 60000 .

387.title: Jackett
387.content: type: jackett · version 0.3.1 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . The configured indexers and how many of them failed on their last search (marked), as homepage’s jackett widget. key is the API Key at the top of Jackett’s page. When Jackett has an Admin password set, give it as password too. Learn more about Jackett.

388.title: Display fields
388.content: configured, errored . Pick them with fields: in the entry.

389.title: Configuration options
389.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | url | url | yes |   | E.g. http://jackett.lan:9117 | . | key | string | yes |   | Secret: stays on the server. The API Key at the top of Jackett’s page | . | password | string |   |   | Secret: stays on the server. The admin password, when one is set | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

390.title: Filter attributes
390.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | configured | number | Indexers configured | . | errored | number | Configured indexers whose last search failed | . | attention | boolean | True while the card marks something as needing attention | .

391.title: Example
391.content: # services.yaml - Downloads: - Jackett: href: http://jackett.lan:9117 icon: jackett widget: type: jackett fields: [configured, errored] # the display fields; leave out for the defaults url: http://jackett.lan:9117 key: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_JACKETT_KEY}}" password: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_JACKETT_PASSWORD}}" # only with an admin password .

393.title: JDownloader
393.content: type: jdownloader · version 0.4.1 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . The packages in JDownloader’s download list, their total size, what is left to download and the download rate, as homepage’s jdownloader widget. Like homepage it goes through My.JDownloader: connect JDownloader to your account under Settings > My.JDownloader, then fill in the account’s e-mail address and password and the device name shown there as client. JDownloader needs no open port for this. Learn more about JDownloader.

394.title: Display fields
394.content: downloadCount, downloadTotalBytes, downloadBytesRemaining, downloadSpeed . Pick them with fields: in the entry.

395.title: Configuration options
395.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | username | string | yes |   | The e-mail address of your My.JDownloader account | . | password | string | yes |   | Secret: stays on the server. | . | client | string | yes |   | The device name of the JDownloader instance (Settings > My.JDownloader) | . | url | url |   | https://api.jdownloader.org | Only for another My.JDownloader server | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

396.title: Filter attributes
396.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | downloadCount | number | Packages in the download list | . | downloadBytesRemaining | number | Still to download over all packages, in GB | . | downloadSpeed | number | Download speed of the running packages, in MB/s | .

397.title: Example
397.content: # services.yaml - Downloads: - JDownloader: href: https://my.jdownloader.org/ icon: jdownloader widget: type: jdownloader fields: [downloadCount, downloadTotalBytes, downloadBytesRemaining, downloadSpeed] # the display fields; leave out for the defaults username: anna@example.com password: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_MYJD_PASSWORD}}" client: JDownloader@nas .

399.title: Jellyfin
399.content: type: jellyfin · version 0.3.0 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . What is playing on Jellyfin, one row per stream with its position and a progress bar (paused streams get a pause icon), as homepage’s jellyfin widget. With enableBlocks: true it also shows the number of movies, series, episodes, songs and albums; enableNowPlaying: false leaves the streams out. Pausing a stream from the card (homepage’s enableMediaControl) is not offered: the widgets only read. Make an API key in Jellyfin under Dashboard > API Keys (Jellyfin 10.12: Administration > Dashboard > Advanced > API Keys). homepage’s version: 2 is accepted but not needed. Learn more about Jellyfin.

400.title: Display fields
400.content: movies, series, episodes, songs, albums . Pick them with fields: in the entry.

401.title: Configuration options
401.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | url | url | yes |   | E.g. http://jellyfin.lan:8096 | . | key | string | yes |   | Secret: stays on the server. Dashboard > API Keys | . | enableNowPlaying | boolean |   | true | A row per stream that is playing | . | enableBlocks | boolean |   | false | Movies, series, episodes, songs and albums | . | enableUser | boolean |   | false | The user’s name after the title | . | showEpisodeNumber | boolean |   | false | S01 · E02 in episode titles | . | version | number |   | 1 | Homepage’s option for Jellyfin 10.12; not needed here (both versions work) | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

402.title: Filter attributes
402.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | streams | number | Streams playing now | .

403.title: Example
403.content: # services.yaml - Media: - Jellyfin: href: http://jellyfin.lan:8096 icon: jellyfin widget: type: jellyfin fields: [movies, series, episodes, songs, albums] # the display fields; leave out for the defaults url: http://jellyfin.lan:8096 key: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_JELLYFIN_KEY}}" enableBlocks: true enableUser: true showEpisodeNumber: true .

441.title: Kubernetes pods
441.content: type: kubernetes-pods · version 1.3.0 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . State, CPU and memory of an app’s pods, as in homepage. This is the widget behind a service’s app: (with namespace: and optionally podSelector:): the state shows as a label in the card’s corner (running, partial when only some pods run, which is marked), and a click on it shows the pods, CPU and memory. Discovered Ingresses and routes get it too, with their own name as app (the app, pod-selector and external annotations change that). app matches pods labelled app.kubernetes.io/name=<app>; podSelector takes any label selector instead (app.kubernetes.io/instance in (synapse, element); an empty one selects every pod in the namespace). CPU is a share of the pods’ CPU limits when they have them, else cores. external: true on a service leaves the label out. The connection is the one of kubernetes.yaml (see Discovery). Give the account read access to pods and their metrics, and install metrics-server for CPU and memory: . rules: - apiGroups: [""] resources: ["pods"] verbs: ["list"] - apiGroups: ["metrics.k8s.io"] resources: ["pods"] verbs: ["list"] . Learn more about Kubernetes labels.

442.title: Display fields
442.content: status, pods, cpu, mem . Pick them with fields: in the entry.

443.title: Configuration options
443.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | namespace | string |   | default |   | . | app | string |   |   | Matches pods labelled app.kubernetes.io/name= | . | podSelector | string |   |   | A label selector instead of app, e.g. app.kubernetes.io/instance in (a, b) | . | url | url |   |   | The API server, e.g. https://k8s.lan:6443 | . | token | string |   |   | Secret: stays on the server. | . | username | string |   |   | Secret: stays on the server. | . | password | string |   |   | Secret: stays on the server. | . | tlsCa | string |   |   | Secret: stays on the server. PEM text of the cluster’s CA | . | tlsCert | string |   |   | Secret: stays on the server. PEM text of a client certificate | . | tlsKey | string |   |   | Secret: stays on the server. PEM text of its key | . | insecure | boolean |   | false | Skip the certificate check (insecure-skip-tls-verify) | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

444.title: Filter attributes
444.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | serviceStatus | string | Up or down, as the status label | . | status | string | The pods’ state: running, partial, not running or not found | . | cpu | number | CPU the pods use, in % of their limits; in cores when they have no limits | . | mem | number | Memory the pods use, in GB (the card shows MB below 1 GB); null without metrics-server | . | attention | boolean | True while the card marks something as needing attention | .

445.title: Example
445.content: # services.yaml - Media: - Jellyfin: href: https://jellyfin.lan namespace: media app: jellyfin # pods labelled app.kubernetes.io/name=jellyfin - Chat: href: https://chat.lan namespace: comms app: matrix podSelector: app.kubernetes.io/instance in (synapse, element) - Grafana pods: widget: # or as a widget on the card type: kubernetes-pods fields: [status, pods, cpu, mem] # the display fields; leave out for the defaults namespace: monitoring app: grafana .

447.title: Kubernetes
447.content: type: kubernetes · version 1.3.1 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . CPU and memory of a Kubernetes cluster (the one the dashboard runs in, or with mode: default in kubernetes.yaml the one in its kubeconfig): the cluster as a whole, and a line per node (a node that is not Ready is marked). Capacity is the nodes’ allocatable CPU and memory; usage comes from metrics-server, so install that first (without it the usage shows as –). The dashboard uses its pod’s service account, or with mode: default the kubeconfig’s user (see Discovery); the dashboard then fills in url, token and the certificates itself. Give that account read access to nodes and their metrics: . apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: ClusterRole metadata: { name: dashboard-nodes } rules: - apiGroups: [""] resources: ["nodes"] verbs: ["get", "list"] - apiGroups: ["metrics.k8s.io"] resources: ["nodes"] verbs: ["get", "list"] . Bind it to the dashboard’s service account with a ClusterRoleBinding, as for discovery. Learn more about Kubernetes.

PEM text of the cluster’s CA | . | tlsCert | string |   |   | Secret: stays on the server. PEM text of a client certificate | . | tlsKey | string |   |   | Secret: stays on the server. PEM text of its key | . | insecure | boolean |   | false | Skip the certificate check (insecure-skip-tls-verify) | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

450.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | cpu | number | CPU in use, in % of what the nodes can allocate | . | memory | number | Memory in use, in % of what the nodes can allocate | . | nodes | number | Nodes in the cluster | . | ready | number | Nodes that are ready | .

469.title: Longhorn
469.content: type: longhorn · version 0.3.1 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . 648.title: OpenWrt
648.content: type: openwrt · version 0.4.0 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . An OpenWrt router’s uptime and 5-minute load average, or with interfaceName (a device such as eth0 or br-lan) that interface’s state (marked when down) and the bytes sent and received, as homepage’s openwrt widget. The widget talks to ubus over /ubus, which needs a user with a read ACL. Create /usr/share/rpcd/acl.d/dashboard.json: . { "dashboard": { "description": "Dashboard", "read": { "ubus": { "network.device": ["status"], "system": ["info"] } } } } . make a password hash with uhttpd -m "<password>", and add the user to /etc/config/rpcd: . config login option username 'dashboard' option password '<the hash>' list read dashboard . then service rpcd restart. Learn more about OpenWrt.

Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

726.title: Prometheus Metric
726.content: type: prometheusmetric · version 0.2.0 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . The results of up to four PromQL queries, each with your own label, as homepage’s prometheusmetric widget. Each entry of metrics has a label, a query (the first result of a vector, or a scalar, is shown) and optionally a key (for fields) and a format: . | type: text (default), number, percent, bytes, bits, byterate, bitrate, duration (seconds as a span), relativeDate (milliseconds, as a span from now) or date (milliseconds). homepage’s binary types (bbytes, bibyterate, …) show decimal units, as everywhere in this collection. | scale: a number, or a fraction such as 1/16, to multiply by. | prefix and suffix: text before and after the value. | options.maximumFractionDigits for number and percent. | . The widget refreshes every 10 seconds; set refreshInterval (milliseconds) on the entry for another rate. Fill in username and password when Prometheus sits behind basic authentication. Learn more about querying Prometheus.

727.title: Display fields
727.content: The blocks are the metrics you configure: fields takes their key (or label). Pick them with fields: in the entry.

728.title: Configuration options
728.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | url | url | yes |   | E.g. http://prometheus.lan:9090 | . | metrics | list | yes |   | [{ label, query, key?, format: { type, scale, prefix, suffix, options } }] | . | username | string |   |   | When Prometheus sits behind basic authentication | . | password | string |   |   | Secret: stays on the server. | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

729.title: Example
729.content: # services.yaml - Monitoring: - Prometheus: href: http://prometheus.lan:9090 icon: prometheus widget: type: prometheusmetric fields: [fields, key, label] # the display fields; leave out for the defaults url: http://prometheus.lan:9090 metrics: - label: Alerts query: count(ALERTS{alertstate="firing"}) or vector(0) - label: Disk free query: node_filesystem_avail_bytes{mountpoint="/"} format: { type: bytes } - label: Uptime query: time() - node_boot_time_seconds format: { type: duration } .

737.title: Proxmox VE
737.content: type: proxmox · version 0.3.0 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . Running and total virtual machines and LXC containers (templates left out), and the CPU and memory in use over the online nodes, as homepage’s proxmox widget. node limits it to one node. For one VM or container on a service’s card, use the dashboard’s own proxmoxNode and proxmoxVMID instead. Make a read-only API token: Datacenter > Permissions > API Tokens > Add (with Privilege Separation checked), then Datacenter > Permissions > Add > API Token Permission with path /, that token and the role PVEAuditor. username is the token id (api@pam!dashboard), password the secret Proxmox shows once. Proxmox uses a self-signed certificate by default, so insecure is on, as in homepage; set insecure: false with a trusted certificate. Learn more about Proxmox VE.

The token’s secret | . | node | string |   |   | Only this node; default the whole cluster | . | insecure | boolean |   | true | Accept Proxmox’s self-signed certificate (as homepage does) | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

749.title: Proxmox VM
749.content: type: proxmoxvm · version 1.3.0 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . State, CPU and memory of one Proxmox VM (QEMU) or LXC container, as in homepage. This is the widget behind a service’s proxmoxNode: and proxmoxVMID: (with proxmoxType: lxc for a container): the state shows as a label in the card’s corner, and a click on it shows CPU and memory. The connection comes from proxmox.yaml (see Configuration), per node or one for every node. A paused VM is marked; a stopped one shows as down. Make a read-only API token in Proxmox: Datacenter > Permissions > API Tokens > Add (with Privilege Separation checked), then Datacenter > Permissions > Add > API Token Permission with path /, that token and the role PVEAuditor. token is the token id (user@pam!dashboard), secret the value Proxmox shows once. Proxmox uses a self-signed certificate by default, so insecure is on, as in homepage. Set insecure: false in proxmox.yaml when Proxmox has a trusted certificate. Learn more about Proxmox VE.

750.content: status, cpu, mem . Pick them with fields: in the entry.

An API token id: user@pam!dashboard | . | secret | string | yes |   | Secret: stays on the server. The token’s secret | . | node | string | yes |   | The Proxmox node name, as proxmoxNode | . | vmid | string | yes |   | The VM or container id, as proxmoxVMID | . | type | qemu / lxc |   | qemu | Qemu for a VM, lxc for a container | . | insecure | boolean |   | true | Accept Proxmox’s self-signed certificate (as homepage does) | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

803.title: System resources
803.content: type: resources · version 1.6.1 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . CPU, memory, disk, CPU temperature, uptime and network as meters, like homepage’s resources widget. 843.title: Shelly
843.content: type: shelly · version 1.2.0 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . A Shelly device’s firmware version and, when a newer one is available, that version in a block marked as needing attention, with an Update firmware button under the blocks that starts it. An up-to-date device shows only its version. While the device updates, the button says the update started; it goes away once the device reports the new version. Works with Gen2, Gen3 and Gen4 devices (the RPC API) and with Gen1 devices. Set password only when the device has authentication on (Settings > Authentication on Gen2 and newer, Internet & Security > Restrict login on Gen1): Gen2 and newer log in as admin with digest authentication, Gen1 with the username and password set there. When the device refuses the password, or asks for one while none is set, the card says so. Fill the password in through {{DASHBOARD_VAR_...}}, not {{...}} alone: an unknown placeholder stays literal and is refused. The widget asks the device to look for new firmware at most once an hour (it also looks by itself); with beta: true a beta version is offered when there is no newer stable one. Anyone who can open the dashboard can press the button: put the dashboard behind authentication before you add it. The device restarts at the end of the update, so the card shows an error for a moment. Learn more about Shelly.

844.content: firmware, update (only when an update is available or being installed) . Pick them with fields: in the entry.

Only when the device has authentication on | . | username | string |   | admin | Gen1 only; Gen2 and newer always use admin | . | beta | boolean |   | false | Also offer beta firmware | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

846.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | update | boolean | True while an update is available or being installed | . | version | string | The installed firmware | . | available | string | The firmware on offer, or null | .

891.title: Stocks
891.content: type: stocks · version 1.3.1 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . The current price and the day’s change of up to eight stocks, from Finnhub. Sign up for a free API key at Finnhub, then put it once in settings.yaml under providers and use provider: finnhub (as in homepage), or set apiKey. The key stays on the server. Up and down are shown with ▲ and ▼; color: false leaves out the green and red. cache keeps the prices for that many minutes (Finnhub’s free tier allows 60 calls a minute, one per symbol). Learn more about Finnhub.

Or provider: finnhub (settings.yaml providers) | . | color | boolean |   | true | Green up, red down (the arrows show it either way) | . | cache | number |   | 1 | Minutes between calls to Finnhub | . 921.title: Tailscale
921.content: type: tailscale · version 0.5.0 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . One device in your tailnet: its Tailscale address, when it was last seen and when its key expires (marked within a week, or when expired), as homepage’s tailscale widget. More through fields: the user, host name, name, client version, operating system, creation date, whether it is authorized (marked when not), external, and has an update available (marked), and its tags. Times show as spans (“2d 3h”). Make an API access token on the keys page (it expires after at most 90 days). The device ID is under the machine’s Machine Details in the machines page and ends in CNTRL. Learn more about Tailscale.

922.title: Display fields
922.content: address, last_seen, expires, user, hostname, name, client_version, os, created, authorized, is_external, update_available, tags . Pick them with fields: in the entry; without it the widget shows address, last_seen, expires.

923.title: Configuration options
923.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | deviceid | string | yes |   | The device’s ID from the admin console (ends in CNTRL) | . | key | string | yes |   | Secret: stays on the server. An API access token: Settings > Keys | . | url | url |   | https://api.tailscale.com | The Tailscale API | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

924.title: Filter attributes
924.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | hostname | string | The device’s host name, such as nas | . | client_version | string | The device’s Tailscale version, such as 1.88.3 | . | os | string | The device’s operating system, such as linux | . | authorized | boolean | True when the device is authorized in the tailnet | . | external | boolean | True when the device is shared in from another tailnet | . | update | boolean | True when a Tailscale update is available for the device | . | hoursSinceSeen | number | Hours since the device was last seen; 0 while connected | . | daysUntilExpiry | number | Days until the device’s key expires; 0 once expired, null when it never does | . | attention | boolean | True while the card marks something as needing attention | .

925.title: Example
925.content: # services.yaml - Network: - Tailscale NAS: href: https://login.tailscale.com/admin/machines icon: tailscale widget: type: tailscale deviceid: n1234567CNTRL key: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_TAILSCALE_KEY}}" fields: [address, last_seen, expires, update_available] .

945.title: Technitium DNS Server
945.content: type: technitium · version 0.3.2 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . The queries a Technitium DNS server answered over the past range (default the last hour), and how many of them were authoritative, cached and server failures (marked), as homepage’s technitium widget (without the share of each: that does not fit a block on a phone). fields also offers no error, NX domain, refused, recursive, blocked, dropped and the clients. Create an API token (best for a user of its own) under Administration > Sessions > Create Token. node picks a cluster node, or cluster for all of them. Learn more about Technitium DNS Server.

946.title: Display fields
946.content: totalQueries, totalNoError, totalServerFailure, totalNxDomain, totalRefused, totalAuthoritative, totalRecursive, totalCached, totalBlocked, totalDropped, totalClients . Pick them with fields: in the entry; without it the widget shows totalQueries, totalAuthoritative, totalCached, totalServerFailure.

947.title: Configuration options
947.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | url | url | yes |   | E.g. http://dns.lan:5380 | . | key | string | yes |   | Secret: stays on the server. An API token (Administration > Sessions > Create Token), best for its own user | . | node | string |   |   | A cluster node’s name, or cluster for all nodes; without it the server asked | . | range | LastHour / LastDay / LastWeek / LastMonth / LastYear |   | LastHour |   | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

948.title: Filter attributes
948.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | totalQueries | number | Queries in the chosen range | . | totalNoError | number | Queries answered without an error | . | totalServerFailure | number | Queries that ended in a server failure | . | totalNxDomain | number | Queries for a domain that does not exist | . | totalRefused | number | Queries refused | . | totalAuthoritative | number | Queries answered from the server’s own zones | . | totalRecursive | number | Queries answered by recursion | . | totalCached | number | Queries answered from the cache | . | totalBlocked | number | Queries blocked | . | totalDropped | number | Queries dropped | . | totalClients | number | Clients that sent queries | . | attention | boolean | True while the card marks something as needing attention | .

949.title: Example
949.content: # services.yaml - Network: - Technitium: href: http://dns.lan:5380 icon: technitium widget: type: technitium fields: [totalQueries, totalNoError, totalServerFailure, totalNxDomain, totalRefused, totalAuthoritative, totalRecursive, totalCached, totalBlocked, totalDropped, totalClients] # the display fields; leave out for the defaults url: http://dns.lan:5380 key: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_TECHNITIUM_TOKEN}}" range: LastDay .

975.title: TrueNAS
975.content: type: truenas · version 0.4.0 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . 993.title: UniFi Controller
993.content: type: unifi (or unifi_console) · version 0.4.1 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . Uptime, WAN status and the users and devices on LAN and WLAN, from a UniFi Network controller (UniFi OS consoles such as the Dream Machine and Cloud Key, or a self-hosted controller). Without fields it shows uptime, WAN, LAN users and WLAN users, as in homepage; subsystems the controller does not report (no gateway, no access points) are left out, and a subsystem that is down is marked. Sign in with either: . | an API key (UniFi OS 4 and later): Settings › Control Plane › Integrations, put it in key; | or a local account with read access (not a UI.com cloud account): username and password. The widget tries UniFi OS first and falls back to a classic controller. | . site is the site’s name or description as the controller shows it; without it, the default site. Most controllers use a self-signed certificate: set insecure: true to accept it (the connection stays encrypted, but the certificate is not checked). In widgets.yaml the header form also works under homepage’s name, unifi_console. Learn more about UniFi Network.

994.title: Display fields
994.content: uptime, wan, lan, lan_users, lan_devices, wlan, wlan_users, wlan_devices . Pick them with fields: in the entry; without it the widget shows uptime, wan, lan_users, wlan_users.

995.title: Configuration options
995.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | url | url | yes |   | E.g. https://unifi.lan (UniFi OS) or https://unifi.lan:8443 | . | site | string |   |   | The site’s name or description; default: the default site | . | key | string |   |   | Secret: stays on the server. An API key (UniFi OS: Settings > Control Plane > Integrations), or: | . | username | string |   |   | A local account with read access | . | password | string |   |   | Secret: stays on the server. | . | insecure | boolean |   | false | True: accept the controller’s self-signed certificate | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

996.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | status | string | Up or down, as the status label | . | wan | string | The WAN’s state, such as up or down | . | lan | string | The LAN’s state, such as up or down | . | lan_users | number | Clients on the LAN, guests included | . | lan_devices | number | Switches adopted | . | wlan | string | The WLAN’s state, such as up or down | . | wlan_users | number | Clients on the WLAN, guests included | . | wlan_devices | number | Access points adopted | . | uptimeHours | number | Hours since the gateway started | . | attention | boolean | True while the card marks something as needing attention | .
